doppel · a report on its own source

doppel

doppel measures architectural erosion in a Go codebase — the widening gap between the structure a project intends and the one it actually has.

Open the report doppel's own source ›

Not a demo corpus: the tool's own source, analysed by itself and regenerated from master on every push. Every pair it names can be opened in the repository and judged — which is the only honest way to show a similarity tool working. One self-contained file, nothing to fetch.

What you are looking at

Map draws the corpus as a political map. Each package is a polygon whose area is its share of the functions, so the picture is a cartogram rather than a floor plan. Each region is tinted by the concept doppel learned from this corpus — rather than from a fixed list — that most of its functions carry. A painted border between two regions is duplication crossing it — the heavier the paint, the more of it.

Neighbourhood takes one function and ranks everything similar to it, with both bodies side by side and the evidence underneath: the two similarity scores kept deliberately unblended, the structural motifs the pair actually shares, and the callers, callees and packages that corroborate the match.

Nothing on the page is a verdict. Doppel measures a codebase against its own practice, so what it reports is "this repo has two of these" — whether that is worth merging is a judgment it does not make.
